notes: §1985:VI.5.9.4 GR1: 'There are five categories of data that can be described with a PICTURE clause: alphabetic, numeric, alphanumeric, alphanumeric edited, and numeric edited.' PictureAnalyzer.AnalyzeCharacterString sorts every character-string into exactly these at 85: the A/X arm gives PicCategory.Alphanumeric (IsAlphabetic when the string is all 'A', an EditMask when B 0 / make it alphanumeric edited), the editing-symbol arm gives NumericEdited and the fall-through arm Numeric. The three categories 2023 adds define no item at 85: a PICTURE of N, 1 or E is still analysed, and VersionConformancePass.GateDataItem (UsageConstructId for national-data-2002 and boolean-data-2002, PictureConstructId for pic-external-float-2002 and national-edited-2002) refuses the entry with COBOL0900 below 2002. Probed at --std 85: PIC NN, PIC 11 and PIC 9.9E+99 each get COBOL0900. The witness declares one item of each of the five categories and displays them.

next.reason: 1985: 'There are five categories of data that can be described with a PICTURE clause: alphabetic, numeric, alphanumeric, alphanumeric edited, and numeric edited.' §2023:13.18.40.4 GR3 lists eight: the five plus boolean, national and national-edited, so PICTURE strings of '1' or 'N' (not 1985 symbols, refused) now define items. Its BWZ sentence was already 1985 law (VI.5.4.4 GR2).
